summary: Type B of the Chinese Government Scholarship, also called the University Program, is run through Chinese universities. A student first applies to a participating university for a master's or doctoral place; the university then nominates its best candidates to the China Scholarship Council (CSC), whose experts make the final decision. Awards cover tuition, accommodation and a monthly allowance with medical insurance, and the details differ from one university to the next. Each university sets its own dates, programme list, language requirements and agency number.
eligibility_notes:
The scholarship is for non-Chinese citizens who hold a valid foreign passport, are in good physical and mental health, and obey Chinese law. Applicants must meet the admission rules of the university they apply to; the nomination does not replace that application.

Master's applicants need a bachelor's degree with an excellent academic record, and doctoral applicants need a master's degree with an excellent record. Final-year students may apply but must hold the graduation certificate and degree diploma before enrolling; if they cannot show them at registration, admission and the scholarship are cancelled (SUFE, BFSU).

Age: generally under 35 for master's and under 40 for doctoral study (SUFE, BFSU, SISU).

Language at SUFE: for English-taught programmes, TOEFL iBT 80 or above, IELTS Academic 6.5 or above, or Duolingo English Test 110 or above; for Chinese-taught programmes, HSK Level 5 with a score of at least 180. BFSU asks for HSK and/or IELTS (or equivalent) according to the school and major, and applicants who earned a degree taught in Chinese at a Chinese university need no HSK report. Other universities set their own scores.

Other conditions: BFSU asks for good conduct with no record of law or public security violations, and a health check that would pass for a Chinese visa or residence permit. A holder of another government or institutional scholarship cannot receive a second award at the same time, except one-off lump-sum awards (BFSU, SISU). Hiding other funding can lead to cancellation, repayment and a three-year ban on applying (BFSU, SISU). A winner who has offers from several universities receives only one scholarship (SUFE). Applicants who are not nominated are considered for self-funded places at SUFE.
age_experience_notes: Master's applicants are generally under 35 and doctoral applicants under 40 (SUFE, BFSU, SISU). The pages read do not state any work experience requirement.
funding_summary: Type B generally gives a tuition waiver, accommodation (a university dormitory or a housing subsidy), a monthly living allowance and medical insurance, for the normal length of the programme. Stipend examples: CNY 3,000 per month for master's and CNY 3,500 per month for doctoral students (SUFE, BFSU, NWPU). Funding length at SUFE is 2 academic years for master's and 3 or 4 for doctoral, set at admission; BFSU lists 2, 3 or 4 years from 1 September 2027. Travel to China is paid by the student at BFSU. Partial awards exist: NWPU says a partial award covers one or some of tuition, dormitory, stipend and insurance.
programmes_note: Only graduate programmes (master's and doctoral) appear in the university notices read, and each university decides which of its programmes take Type B students. Teaching language is Chinese and/or English depending on the programme. NWPU says only certain majors qualify and some carry extra limits. SISU says applicants must choose from its 2026 graduate programme list, with a separate Silk Road sub-programme for nationals of Belt and Road partner countries in fields it designates. The programme names themselves are on each university's own list, which the notices point to but the pages read do not reproduce.
institutions_note: Type B is delivered by the participating Chinese universities, each of which receives applications under its own CSC agency number. Examples read: Peking University (10001), Beijing Foreign Studies University (10030), Shanghai University of Finance and Economics (10272), Northwestern Polytechnical University (10699). The CSC decides the host university of a winner, and a winner may not change university, field, language of instruction or study length afterwards. No single official list of all universities could be read.

summary.detail: Master's study. Funding length 2 academic years at SUFE; BFSU lists 2, 3 or 4 year periods from 1 September 2027 without saying which applies to master's; NWPU supports the length required by the programme; SISU and PKU list 2 to 3 years. Teaching language Chinese and/or English depending on the programme. Entry: bachelor's degree with an excellent record, generally under 35. Stipend CNY 3,000 per month.

Doctoral study. Funding length 3 or 4 academic years at SUFE, set at admission; SISU and PKU list 4 years (PKU also 4 to 5). Teaching language Chinese and/or English depending on the programme. Entry: master's degree with an excellent record, generally under 40. Stipend CNY 3,500 per month.

benefits.limit_text: Tuition waiver; full tuition waiver at SUFE; at PKU full or partial
benefits.conditions: Partial awards cover only some items at NWPU. Duration follows the programme's normal length.

benefits.limit_text: On-campus accommodation fees at SUFE; free BFSU housing, or a rent subsidy of RMB 700 per month (master's) or RMB 1,000 per month (doctoral) if renting in China; university dormitory or accommodation subsidy at NWPU
benefits.conditions: Housing is given only where the scholarship covers it.

benefits.limit_text: CNY 3,000 per month for master's and CNY 3,500 per month for doctoral students
benefits.conditions: At NWPU a student who registers by the 15th of a month gets the full monthly amount and one who registers after the 15th gets half; the stipend is suspended if the student stays outside China more than 15 days for personal reasons (school holidays excluded).

benefits.limit_text: Comprehensive medical insurance; NWPU states CNY 800 per person per year
benefits.conditions: Cover applies in China during the study period.

benefits.limit_text: International travel costs are paid by the student (BFSU)
benefits.conditions: Stated by BFSU; other notices read do not mention travel.

requirements.text: Application to the host university through its own online application system, with the university's application fee where one is charged (SUFE: CNY 830 or CNY 1,660; the notice does not say which amount applies to which level). All files are colour scans of originals; no paper copies at this stage (SUFE).
Conditional offer or pre-admission notice from the university, which is uploaded when applying in the CSC Chinese Government Scholarship Information System together with the CSC application form.
First page of a valid ordinary passport, valid beyond September of the entry year (BFSU).

Notarised diploma, pre-graduation certificate or degree certificate, in Chinese or English; others need a notarised translation (BFSU). PKU asks for CSCSE or CSSD authentication for graduation and degree certificates.
Academic transcript, with a notarised Chinese or English translation if in another language (BFSU).
Chinese and/or English proficiency certificate as the programme requires (SUFE: TOEFL iBT 80, IELTS 6.5, Duolingo 110 or HSK 5 with 180).
requirements.conditional_rule: Not needed by applicants whose degree was earned in Chinese at a Chinese university (BFSU) or whose first language is English where the university allows it

requirements.text: Personal statement and a student affirmation signed by the applicant (BFSU).
Two recommendation letters from associate professors or higher, in Chinese or English (BFSU); PKU asks for two letters from professors or associate professors.

Research proposal of more than 1,500 words for master's or more than 3,000 words for doctoral applicants (BFSU); PKU states a personal statement with research plan of 1,500 words (master's) or 3,000 words (doctoral).
Physical Examination Record for Foreigners completed in English and valid for 6 months (BFSU).
Non-criminal record report issued within 6 months before the application date (BFSU).
Residence or stay certificate or visa page, certificate of enrolment, a transfer or withdrawal certificate, and a recommendation letter and transcript from the current university (BFSU).
requirements.conditional_rule: Only applicants who are currently studying in China

application_steps.title: Apply to the Chinese university first
application_steps.detail: Choose a participating university and its master's or doctoral programme, and apply in that university's own online system. Select Type B (university scholarship) where the form asks, upload scans, and pay the application fee if one applies. Dates vary: SUFE took applications from 16 November 2025 to 28 February 2026 for the 2026 intake, BFSU until 31 January 2027 for the 2027 intake, and NWPU in two batches (1 November to 31 December 2026, then 1 January to 28 February 2027, deadlines at 17:00 Beijing time).

application_steps.title: Pass the university's review and get a conditional offer
application_steps.detail: The university checks documents, may run an academic review, exam or interview, and then issues a conditional offer or pre-admission notice. At SUFE only applicants with a conditional offer may apply for the scholarship. NWPU describes two rounds of document review, an interview and an overall assessment.

application_steps.title: Apply in the CSC scholarship system
application_steps.detail: With the offer in hand, log in to the Chinese Government Scholarship Information System, choose scholarship category Type B, enter the university's agency number, and submit the online form with the offer and other required files. BFSU's window for 2027 entry runs from 5 January to 28 February 2027; SUFE opened its stage in late March 2026. Save the application form and, where the university asks, send the CSC serial number to it (NWPU).

application_steps.title: University nominates candidates to the CSC
application_steps.detail: The university reviews the CSC applications and sends its recommended candidates to the China Scholarship Council, in batches at NWPU. BFSU posts a recommended-candidates list on its website; the list is informational only and unselected candidates are not told individually. Applicants who are not nominated are considered for self-funded study at SUFE.

application_steps.title: CSC experts take the final decision
application_steps.detail: CSC and designated experts check eligibility and academic performance and decide who receives the award; the CSC also decides the host university. SISU says it assesses academic performance, overall quality and future potential, and that an applicant who fails the expert review has no second chance in that application cycle. Results come in about late June to July (SUFE).

application_steps.title: Receive admission papers and enrol
application_steps.detail: SUFE emails winners and sends the admission package (Admission Notice, Confirmation Form for Study in China, JW201 form) in late June or July; BFSU mails the admission documents to the address given in its system. Winners apply for a study visa and register on the registration day in the Admission Notice (September at SUFE), bringing originals for checking. Late registration cancels admission and the scholarship; BFSU and SUFE also require the final graduation and degree certificates at registration.

application_steps.title: Keep the award while studying
application_steps.detail: Winners may not change host university, field, language of instruction or study length after enrolment (SUFE, BFSU, SISU). They must pass any annual scholarship review (SISU), may not hold another government or institutional scholarship at the same time, and false documents or hidden funding lead to cancellation, repayment and a ban of three years on applying (BFSU, SISU).
